newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Directors must focus on performance - AICD.
newsitem.headline: Directors must focus on performance - AICD.

text.p: Company directors needed to intensify the focus on the performance aspect of their role rather than traditional functions of a director, the Australian Institute of Company Directors (AICD) was told on Monday.

Launching "Future Direction-The Power of the Competitive Board", a study of the effectiveness of company directors, Sir Bruce Watson, chairman of the institute's Competitive Board Project Advisory Committee, said conformance responsibilities were hindering company performance.
"Our concern was that increasing regulation and accent on governance - the conformance role of directors - was detracting from accent on company performance," he told an institute luncheon.
"We believed that the performance role of the board was vital."

The book's author, Ivor S. Francis of the Deming Centre International, said in measuring the capabilities of company directors to perform their duties, Australia directors had been judged to be only 70 percent effective.
"This study demonstrates that the traditional functions of directing, by themselves, have little apparent direct influence on the performance of the company," Francis said.

"On the other hand, the assuring function of directing, which includes understanding the company's business, assigning accountabilities, building relationships with management and actively assuring the health of of financial and operational management, have been shown beyond doubt to have a major influence on the performance of the company."
To improve performance, AICD national president John Ralph said the institute was calling for changes in the Corporations Law to allow directors to make competitive decisions.

"Notable among these is the need for a business judgement rule to provide a 'safe harbour' for directors who take decisions in good faith and on reasonable grounds and in the absence of a conflict of interest," Ralph said, adding that such a rule would enhance certainty for directors and positively influence performance.

"I would hope it would be something that would be brought in in a review of the Act. The Treasurer has expressed that, subject to ensuring it could be done, it was a concept he would favour," Ralph told reporters after the luncheon, saying the current focus was pushing directors to be too cautious.
"You don't want a situation where people can second guess decisions that were made in good faith," Ralph said.
